comments.author: @allzuckedup
comments.text: Greetings from the Denver area.  It's a pretty and romantic video about my home... BUT, a few thoughts, when you're talking about what's in the north, south, east, and west of the state, you were losing me. The mountains in the north that absolutely do look like paintings, but are absolutely not "gentle", it's one of the most harsh environments on earth, and southern, western, and central Colorado have BIG, noteworthy mountain ranges too. When you talk about southern Colorado you were also clearly showing video of Monument Valley on the Arizona/Utah border. And, just a few minutes later, you're showing Red Rocks Amphitheater, while going on about how it's naturally occurring, and only had nature to plan it. That was a Great Depression "New Deal" project from the 1930's, those seats, parking, roads, and the little tunnel at the top didn't carve themselves out of the mountain.  OK, I'm done whining, but I'm only 6 minutes in. Folks, if you want to really see Colorado/the Rockies, do some real talking to folks about where, it is big. Cheers.
